section: India - Scheduled Tribe population: distribution, major tribes and tribal regions
subsections: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)
Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342
ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s: The Elwin Committee (1959) was associated with which of the following?
o: Socio-economic and educational status of tribes
accepted.x: The Elwin Committee was constituted in 1959 and focused on Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive subject.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: The U.N. Dhebar Commission was primarily concerned with which of the following issues?
o: Reservation of seats in State Assemblies
accepted.x: The U.N. Dhebar Commission of 1960–61 examined tribal conditions and land alienation. It also identified least-developed tribal groups and contributed to the later PTG category.
accepted.tq: Direct committee–focus recall.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: Which one of the following committees was associated with the criteria for specifying Scheduled Tribes?
accepted.x: The Lokur Committee, constituted in 1965, dealt with the criteria for specifying Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Confusable committee discrimination.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: The Bhuria Committee is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Creation of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Definition of Scheduled Tribes under Article 366
Identification of Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
Extension of Panchayats to Scheduled Areas leading to PESA
accepted.x: The Bhuria Committee recommended extending Panchayats to Scheduled Areas, a recommendation that led to the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, or PESA.
accepted.tq: Link the recommendation with its legislative outcome.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: The High-Level Committee headed by Virginius Xaxa examined the following subject:
o: Land revenue administration in Scheduled Areas
Socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities
accepted.x: The Virginius Xaxa High-Level Committee, constituted in 2013–14, examined the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities.
accepted.tq: Direct focus recall from a committee label.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kaka Kalelkar Commission:
1. It was set up in 1953.
2. It was constituted under Article 340.
3. It held that tribes lead a separate and exclusive existence and may follow any religion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was set up in 1953 under Article 340 and made the stated observations about tribal existence and religion.
accepted.tq: Use the article, year and finding as separate checks.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the criteria associated with the Lokur Committee for specifying Scheduled Tribes?
accepted.x: The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large and backwardness. Advanced urbanisation is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a characteristic list.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Fifth Schedule from the Sixth Schedule?
o: The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas, whereas the Sixth Schedule deals with tribal areas having autonomous districts or regions.
The Fifth Schedule deals with autonomous districts, whereas the Sixth Schedule deals with ordinary districts.
The Sixth Schedule deals only with tribal welfare grants.
Both Schedules apply exclusively to the north-eastern States.
accepted.x: The Fifth Schedule concerns Scheduled Areas, while the Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous districts and regions in specified north-eastern States.
accepted.tq: Contrast the area type before considering the States.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Sixth Schedule?
accepted.x: The Sixth Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha is among the Fifth Schedule States.
accepted.tq: Separate the four Sixth Schedule States from the Fifth Schedule group.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: How many States are listed as having Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas?
accepted.x: The ten States are Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Count the members of the constitutional list.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Fifth Schedule?
o: Governor's special powers and Tribes Advisory Council
President's direct administration of every tribal village
Exclusive jurisdiction of the Union Public Service Commission
accepted.x: The Fifth Schedule provides for the Governor's special powers and a Tribes Advisory Council in relation to Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Match the Schedule with its constitutional machinery.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s:
With reference to the Tribes Advisory Council, consider the following statements:
1. It may have up to 20 members.
2. About three-fourths of its members are Scheduled Tribe legislators.
3. The President may direct its constitution in a State having Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. A Tribes Advisory Council may have up to 20 members, about three-fourths of whom are ST MLAs, and the President may direct its constitution in a State with STs but no Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Check composition, numerical limit and exceptional power separately.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: The constitutional provision relating to autonomous districts in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram is:
accepted.x: Article 244(2) applies the Sixth Schedule provisions concerning autonomous districts to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Article 244(1) of the Constitution is associated with:
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
The Fifth Schedule and Scheduled Areas
The Sixth Schedule and autonomous districts
Reserved seats in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: Article 244(1) applies the Fifth Schedule provisions relating to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Article–subject matching.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which Article provides grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and the administration of Scheduled Areas?
accepted.x: Article 275(1) provides for grants-in-aid for ST welfare and the administration of Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Identify the function attached to the constitutional article.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes derives its constitutional basis from:
accepted.x: Article 338A provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. It was created through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
accepted.tq: Avoid the look-alike Article 338 and 338A pair.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 is associated with the establishment of the:
accepted.x: The 89th Amendment Act, 2003 provided for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A.
accepted.tq: Link an amendment number with the institution it created.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Under Article 342(1), Scheduled Tribes in a State or Union Territory are notified by the:
o: Governor, after approval by the Supreme Court
President, after consultation with the Governor where applicable
accepted.x: Under Article 342(1), the President specifies the Scheduled Tribes for each State or Union Territory after consulting the Governor in the case of a State.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the constitutional notification function.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Article 342 is correct?
o: A State Legislature can independently alter the ST list for that State.
Only an Act of Parliament can include or exclude a community from the notified ST list.
The ST list is identical for every State and Union Territory.
The Governor alone issues the final ST notification.
accepted.x: Article 342(2) provides that only Parliament may alter the notified list by law. The lists are specific to each State or Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Use the authority and State-specific nature as the decisive clues.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to:
accepted.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes with reference to the communities notified under Article 342.
accepted.tq: Match the definitional provision with the notification provision.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about PESA is correct?
o: It extends Panchayati Raj provisions to Scheduled Areas, and nine of the ten Fifth Schedule States have framed rules, while Odisha has drafts.
It applies only to the four Sixth Schedule States and abolishes autonomous councils.
It provides that Scheduled Tribes cannot receive representation in Panchayats.
It is a constitutional amendment that created Article 342.
accepted.x: PESA extends Panchayat provisions to Scheduled Areas. The stated position is that nine of the ten Fifth Schedule States have framed rules, while Odisha has drafts.
accepted.tq: Identify the law from its operational scope and implementation detail.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: According to the stated provision under Article 164(1), a separate tribal-welfare minister is provided in which group of States?
o: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan
accepted.x: Article 164(1), through its proviso, provides for a separate tribal-welfare minister in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Bihar was dropped by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006.
accepted.tq: Use exact membership and detect the substituted State.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: Which one of the following constitutional amendments dropped Bihar from the States requiring a separate tribal-welfare minister under Article 164(1)?
accepted.x: The 94th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2006 dropped Bihar from the relevant Article 164(1) provision.
accepted.tq: Distinguish amendment numbers by the specific constitutional change.
accepted.sec: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

accepted.s: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 is significant because:
o: It defined the criteria for tribal development blocks.
It transferred the power of notification from the President to Governors.
It forms the base notified list of Scheduled Tribes, which can be changed only by an amending Act of Parliament.
It created the Sixth Schedule autonomous councils.
accepted.x: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 provides the base ST lists. Any subsequent inclusion or exclusion requires an amending Act of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal instrument and its amendment rule.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated criteria traditionally associated with identification of Scheduled Tribes?
o: Shyness of contact with the community at large
Majority representation in urban local bodies
accepted.x: The stated criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness. Majority representation in urban local bodies is not a criterion.
accepted.tq: Find the modern administrative phrase that does not belong to the traditional criteria.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s: Which of the following communities was included in the Scheduled Tribe list of Jammu and Kashmir in 1991, according to the stated classification?
accepted.x: Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Sippis were added to the Jammu and Kashmir ST list in 1991. The Pahari ethnic group, Paddari tribe, Koli and Gadda Brahmin were later additions under the 2024 amendment.
accepted.tq: Separate the earlier inclusion group from the later amendment group.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to additions to the Scheduled Tribe list of Jammu and Kashmir:
1. Pahari ethnic group — 2024
2. Paddari tribe — 2024
3. Gadda Brahmin — 1991
4. Sippis — 1991
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Pahari ethnic group and Paddari tribe were included in 2024, while Sippis were among the communities added in 1991. Gadda Brahmin was included in the 2024 group, not in 1991.
accepted.tq: Split a chronology-based list into the two amendment groups.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of constitution:
A. Lokur Committee
B. Kaka Kalelkar Commission
C. U.N. Dhebar Commission
D. Elwin Committee
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953), Elwin Committee (1959), U.N. Dhebar Commission (1960–61) and Lokur Committee (1965).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest years first, then resolve the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

accepted.s:
A proposal for a new ST (Valley) tier in Assam was reported to cover which of the following communities?
1. Chutia
2. Koch-Rajbongshi
3. Matak
4. Moran
5. Tai Ahom
6. Tea Tribes
accepted.x: The proposed ST (Valley) tier covered all six listed communities: Chutia, Koch-Rajbongshi, Matak, Moran, Tai Ahom and Tea Tribes. Tribal bodies opposed the proposal.
accepted.tq: Treat every named member as a separate list-checking statement.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s: The Assam proposal for a new ST (Valley) tier was made by a:
accepted.x: A Group of Ministers proposed the new ST (Valley) tier for six Assam communities in a report referred to in November 2025.
accepted.tq: Identify the recommending authority rather than the beneficiary communities.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the proposed Assam ST (Valley) tier?
o: It concerned only the four Sixth Schedule States.
It was enacted directly by a State notification without parliamentary action.
It was unanimously accepted by all tribal bodies.
It was proposed for six communities, but tribal bodies opposed it.
accepted.x: The proposal covered six Assam communities, but tribal bodies opposed the creation of the proposed ST (Valley) tier. Inclusion in an ST list ultimately requires the constitutional and parliamentary process.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a proposal and opposition from a completed legal amendment.
accepted.sec: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)
